conviction_note: Two dated, primary-source legal/regulatory items landed in August 2026 and appear in none of the roughly fifteen earnings previews captured for this name, all of which are about Hugo robotics, PFA, the MiniMed separation and tariffs; against a 3.14% median historical reaction I size the pair at about -0.8 points and no more, because the direct dollar amounts are small relative to a ~$116bn market cap and the mechanism (an accrual or call commentary) is probabilistic.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-04 a federal jury in Boston (Judge Patti Saris) returned the first Covidien hernia-mesh bellwether verdict against Medtronic — $88m, $77m to Larry Patterson and $11m to his wife, on failure-to-warn over Symbotex mesh, with no punitives and no fraud finding — and that verdict sits on top of roughly 2,400 federal MDL cases, about 7,450 Massachusetts state cases and a coordinated Minnesota action with no global settlement in place.
findings.why_not_priced: Medtronic filed no 8-K on the verdict — the only filing between 2026-06-18 and the print is a DEFA14A on 2026-08-17 — and no captured earnings preview mentions litigation at all; the FY2026 10-K was filed 2026-06-18, seven weeks before the verdict, so the contingencies note the market last read predates it, and the FQ1 10-Q that follows this print is the first document that has to restate the exposure. If it were priced, the stock would not be sitting 4.6% higher over twenty days with a 21% realised vol and previews framing the quarter as 'confidently ready' for the US robotics push.
findings.independence: A second outlet carried the same verdict independently: https://www.startribune.com/jury-federal-bellwether-medtronic-covidien-mesh-hernia-88-million/601874963 — it appears in the skipped list of snapshots/20260830T152925Z.json with a fetch failure, so I have the URL slug and nothing more, but it is a different publisher naming the same federal bellwether and the same $88m.

findings.finding: FDA issued an Early Alert on Medtronic's and Given Imaging's Bravo esophageal pH monitoring capsule delivery device: Medtronic sent affected customers a quarantine letter on 2026-08-06 and, as of 2026-08-10, had reported 184 serious injuries and no deaths, and separately removed the Harmony pulmonary valve delivery catheter system after a 2026-05-28 customer letter over tip detachment.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a primary FDA page, published three and a half weeks before the print, that no captured preview or sell-side note references; Medtronic filed no 8-K about it. 184 serious injuries is a large enough count to seed follow-on product liability even though the Bravo line is immaterial to revenue, and a company that had seen the market price this would not have gone into the print with previews discussing only growth drivers.
findings.independence: Trade press covered the same recall separately: https://www.medtechdive.com/news/medtronic-recalls-ph-monitoring-capsule-linked-to-184-serious-injuries/829038/ (body stored, docs/2edb580f0dd2d292f6dec88e4ab4151efd4c407e.txt), and the Harmony catheter removal has its own FDA page at https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/medical-device-recalls-and-early-alerts/pulmonary-valve-catheter-delivery-system-recall-medtronic-removes-harmony-delivery-catheter-system

searched_and_found_nothing: a MiniMed separation comparability problem: the diabetes IPO roadshow launched 2026-02-24 and the 424B4 was filed in March 2026, so the recast was already in the numbers when FY27 guidance of 6.75-7.25% organic growth was given on 2026-06-03
a quiet 8-K in the run-in: nothing between the 10-K of 2026-06-18 and the print's own item 2.02, except a routine DEFA14A on 2026-08-17
an insider cluster or a shelf takedown: the S-3ASR is 2026-03-09 with no 424B against it, and no Form 4 wave appears in August
an item 5.02 departure: the last is 2026-05-18, alongside the Q4 print cycle
a Hugo robotics setback: the only Hugo items are positive (510(k) submissions to expand indications, FDA clearance), and they are the centre of the preview copy, i.e. priced
a tariff surprise: the $350m tariff burden and the June guidance raise on lower tariff impact are both in the wire copy and one of the two mddionline pieces on it failed to fetch
a PFA share loss datapoint: the MedTech Dive and survey items say Boston Scientific leads and both names capture the new AF market quickly, which is the consensus view already in print
baseline_tension: My two findings cut mildly against a baseline that shows the stock up 4.6% over twenty days and only 2.4% off its recent level into the print, i.e. no visible discounting of a legal or quality overhang — but they are small enough to sit inside the baseline's 1.57% deadband, so this is a lean, not a call.
corpus_limits: No option chain; the corpus contains two snippet-only investing.com pages ('Medtronic shares may move 4% on Sept 1 earnings release' and one on heavy call buying) that both failed to fetch, so I could not confirm an implied move. The print itself was accepted 2026-09-01T06:47 UTC (02:47 ET), so both 2026-09-01 sweeps (20260901T150553Z and 20260901T152653Z) are post-print; I read only their headline lists to confirm they contained no new pre-print material and used no body from them, and I did not open the item 2.02 8-K accession 0001628280-26-059697 that filings.json indexes. Three documents carry tripwire_tells and I excluded all three: https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/medtronic-stock-draws-fresh-analyst-support-as-fda-alert-tests-sentiment/70010427 , https://stocktwits.com/symbol/MDT/sentiment , https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-medtronic-mdt-expected-to-release-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-08-25/ . I note honestly that the first of those three does discuss both the $88m award and the FDA alert, which means at least one aggregator carried the combination before the print and my 'unpriced' claim is therefore partial rather than absolute. Roughly twenty further URLs, including the Q4 call transcripts and two Seeking Alpha pages, are in the skipped lists with fetch failures.
